claims.reason: Checked the sources. The `hp` step uses `OutgoingDilation.correction_times_U_zero F XR eta X hXR`, which needs only hXR and holds for any X. `hX` is used only through `heatE_times_U` → `heatE_before` → `HeatTailEdit.edit_before`/`switch_zero` (the `0 < X` there serves only to get `0 ≤ X/K` for `Real.log_nonpos`). Definitions: `heatE F XR p = OutgoingDilation.E F XR p * HeatTailEdit.multiplier h ν (switchRadius F XR) p.1`; `multiplier h ν K X = 1 + switch K X * (...)`; `switch K X = OutgoingSchedule.sigma (Real.log (X / K) / (3/10))`; `HeatedOutgoing.U = OutgoingDilation.U`, with `OutgoingDilation.U F XR p = F.U (p.1 / XR, p.2)` and `Profile.U F p = F.logU (Real.log p.1, p.2)`. So both `switch K X` and `U F XR (X, eta)` depend on X only through `Real.log` of a positive multiple of X. Since `Real.log (-x) = Real.log x`, they take the same value at X and at Y = -X. Let K = switchRadius F XR > 0 (by `switchRadius_pos`). Case |X| ≤ K: then 0 ≤ |X|/K ≤ 1, so log ≤ 0 (this includes X = 0, since log 0 = 0), and `sigma_zero` (hypothesis `x ≤ 0`) gives switch = 0. The multiplier is then 1 whatever the `RadialHeatProfile` term is, so heatE = OutgoingDilation.E and the identity holds. Case |X| > K: `U_after_switch F XR eta |X| hXR` gives U(|X|, eta) = 0, so U(X, eta) = 0 and both sides are 0. Without hX the statement stays true and can be proved by a case split, so hX is unnecessary.
